SymbolicEssence.ArchetypalFunction: To embody celestial measurements, seasonal cycles, and the southern pillar of heaven; master of stellar configurations.
SymbolicEssence.SymbolicCore: The cosmic measurer, marker of seasons through stars.

MythicAppearances: Father of Astraeus (stars), Pallas, and Perses
CulturalContext.ReligiousOrRitualUse: Limited direct worship; honored as one of four cosmic pillars; associated with astronomical observation.
CulturalContext.HistoricalEvolution: Obscure Titan associated with celestial mechanics; name means 'ram' connecting to zodiacal symbolism.

SymbolicRepresentation.ImageryNotes: Rarely depicted; when shown, appears as ram-headed or ram-horned titan associated with southern stars and constellations.
SymbolicRepresentation.PoeticInvocation: Ram of the south, pillar of stars, who marks the turning of the cosmic year.
SymbolicRepresentation.DreamForm: A horned figure standing at the south point of the world, around whom the constellations wheel

MetaIntegration.RitualFunction: Invoked for understanding of cosmic cycles, astronomical observation, and seasonal transitions.
AIPromptSeeds: The pillar who measures time by the stars, marking each season's turn.
The ram who stands at the southern gate of heaven.
NarrativeHooks: The steady marker of inevitable cycles
The foundation that cannot be moved
